Subject: Heliodor pilot asks and timeline

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We reviewed the platform with our infra team and have two tight requirements for the pilot/procurement: 1) ability to pin a model variant per-tenant (we need model affinity for regulated workflows) and 2) request-level telemetry that preserves our trace IDs and a route tag so we can reconcile logs across services.

Sincerely,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Heliodor pilot asks and timeline — product/eng assessment requested

Jonas — thanks for the context. Quick clarifying questions before we scope:
1) Does Heliodor require model pinning at tenant granularity, or will route-level/route-tagging be sufficient for their workflows? (tenant-level is more invasive)
2) For telemetry: do they need full traces for every request, or is sampling acceptable during pilot?

Proposed MVP we can evaluate quickly:
- Route-level model affinity flag (configurable per-route in the routing table). This lets them point specific routes to a pinned model variant without a full tenant config surface.
- Runtime metadata pass-through: accept an incoming header (X-Helio-Trace / X-Route-Tag) and ensure the field is emitted into outbound telemetry/trace exporter.

Estimated effort (initial gut check): 3 sprints (~6 weeks) to do production-grade end-to-end: router + config UI + telemetry exporter + QA + perf validation. If we accept a narrower pilot (route-only + header passthrough + sampled telemetry), we can aim for ~4 weeks.

Tradeoffs:
- Tenant-level pinning requires config service schema changes and migration plan — higher risk.
- Emitting every request trace will increase egress and observability cost; sampling helps but reduces fidelity for debugging.

I'll put together a concrete tech approach and a minimal acceptance criteria list.

— Camila
Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Heliodor pilot asks and timeline — product/eng assessment requested

Engineering perspective and proposed approach:

MVP scope that meets Heliodor's procurement ask (minimizes risk):
- Implement a route-level affinity flag in the routing layer (no config service schema changes). Routes can be annotated at deploy-time or via an ops-only toggle. This avoids a tenant migration.
- Add a lightweight runtime metadata passthrough that maps incoming X-Helio-Trace/X-Route-Tag headers to the internal request context and ensures the tracer/exporter includes them in spans/metrics.
- Telemetry: sample at 10% for pilot and export the tag + original trace id to our tracing backend. Provide a CSV export for reconciliation if the customer needs it.

Estimate & resourcing:
- Dedicated engineer (0.5 FTE) + 0.2 QA for 4 weeks to deliver the above (dev + basic perf run + docs).
- Blockers: need a test tenant in staging with traffic simulation, and agreement on header format (we propose X-Helio-Trace).

If Sales can commit to a short-term dev allocation and procurement credits, we can meet the 4-week target. I'll attach a short tech sketch.

— Ben
Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: tech-approach-sketch.md (text)
